trust_decision.summary: Presence state must be held in objects with no prototype chain, because presence keys are chosen on the server and may be "__proto__"/"constructor"/"hasOwnProperty" so the plain existence checks `if(!newState[key])` / `if(!currentPresence)` read inherited members and miss or mis-join entries; but this protection is decided in the JavaScript Presence class, and the pinned commit is the 1.1.3-era tree that contains no JavaScript Presence at all (the first listed commit, 2270aaf, is the one that inserts it at web/static/js/phoenix.js:692 with the flawed checks, while the real fix hunks target assets/js/phoenix.js and assets/js/phoenix/presence.js, paths that do not exist here).

landing_point.why: The summary names Presence and Object.prototype, so an engineer opens the only client source file in the tree and looks for the Presence class; the first listed commit would insert it immediately after Ajax.states (fix.diff:34-103, whose hunk context `Ajax.states = {complete: 4}` is exactly line 692 here), and a case-insensitive search of every file in the pinned tree finds no `presence`, `syncState` or `syncDiff` JavaScript at all.

fix_sites.entry_point: new Phoenix.Presence(channel, opts) - public class constructor, whose instance subscribes to the channel's presence_state/presence_diff events (fix.diff:180)
Presence.syncState(currentState, newState, onJoin, onLeave) - documented static public API (fix.diff:187-189) and the full-state handler behind the instance
Presence.syncDiff(currentState, {joins, leaves}, onJoin, onLeave) - documented static public API and the presence_diff handler behind the instance
Presence.toNullProtoObj(obj) - new helper called by the three sites above

fix_sites.where: assets/js/phoenix/presence.js:11, 69-73, 111, 162-177 (later split-file layout; fix.diff:285-335, replayed identically at fix.diff:391-441 and fix.diff:498-548)
fix_sites.entry_point: the same Presence class in the modular assets/js/phoenix/presence.js - constructor, static syncState, static syncDiff, toNullProtoObj

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exists for this advisory in any one tree: every object indexed by a presence key (the constructor's this.state, syncState's state/newState/joins/leaves, syncDiff's state) lives inside the Presence class and the fix covers all of them, so there is no neighbouring module or second route to argue out of scope - the only separable copy is the generated bundle priv/static/phoenix.js, and at the pinned commit it contains no Presence either.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Presence entries whose key is literally "constructor", "hasOwnProperty" or "__proto__" are legitimate user ids: they must still join, appear in Presence.list() and fire onLeave, and Object.prototype must stay untouched. An over-broad fix that filters, escapes or renames keys colliding with Object.prototype silently drops real users (the fix's own tests require all three keys to join and leave), and replacing the plain state object with a Map breaks the documented lower-level static API that applications call with ordinary objects.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: fix.diff:252-260 (all three colliding keys must join and leave; Object.prototype.metas stays undefined); fix.diff:213-218 (the comment calls Maps a breaking change for the lower-level static API)

O6_input_shapes: "__proto__" as an own property, reachable only through JSON.parse / a JSON round-trip because a "__proto__" key in an object literal sets the prototype instead (fix.diff:242-246)

"constructor" and "hasOwnProperty" - inherited Object.prototype members that make the plain existence check `if(!newState[key])` / `if(!currentPresence)` see a value that was never set (fix.diff:198-199, 244-245)
state passed in with an ordinary prototype versus already null-prototype (toNullProtoObj returns it untouched, fix.diff:220)
full-state synchronisation `syncState(currentState, newState)` versus incremental `syncDiff(state, {joins, leaves})` (fix.diff:189, 203)
keys arriving inside the server's presence_state/presence_diff JSON payload (lib/phoenix/presence.ex:96-101) rather than being constructed in JavaScript

O7_producer.where: lib/phoenix/presence.ex:117-125 (group/1 builds the %{key => %{metas: [...]}} map that the client indexes) plus lib/phoenix/presence.ex:93-102 (the presence_diff broadcast with joins/leaves payload), JSON-encoded on the wire

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same client code in the built bundle that is published as the npm "main"
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: brunch compiles web/static into priv/static/phoenix.js (brunch-config.js:17-30) and package.json publishes only that file (package.json:3, 12), so any presence helper written in web/static has a second generated copy that a fix must regenerate; all the published fix commits touch only assets/js, never priv/static.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-event callback registry keyed by the server-sent event name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the Socket already dispatches raw server events by name (web/static/js/phoenix.js:525-526) and keeps a keyed dispatch table `{open: [], close: [], error: [], message: []}` at line 371; a maintainer adding a cached dispatcher for channel events would naturally index it by the event string and reuse the same `if(!callbacks[event])` existence check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a channel registry keyed by topic instead of the current array
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: channels are looked up linearly with `this.channels.filter(channel => channel.isMember(topic))` (web/static/js/phoenix.js:525) over an array created at line 372; optimising that to `{[topic]: channel}` would key an object by a client-chosen topic string and invite exactly the prototype-collision existence check this advisory is about.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a presence helper shipped in the generated app template, keyed by the server's presence keys
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this template is what every generated Phoenix app starts from and it already wires a channel and its events (socket.js:57-58), so a maintainer adding client presence support to the framework would plausibly show it here as well as inside the library.

O9_family: string-keyed object indexed by a server-chosen key with existence checks that read the Object.prototype chain (CWE-754 improper check for unusual/unexpected conditions; prototype-chain key collision, adjacent to CWE-1321)

O10_build.language: JavaScript browser client inside an Elixir/Phoenix repository
O10_build.toolchain: Node with brunch ^2.1.1 and babel-brunch (package.json:7-11, brunch-config.js:34-37); Elixir 1.2.1 / OTP 18 for the server via mix (.travis.yml:1-6); there is no JavaScript test runner at the pin - mocha and the npm test script are added by the first listed commit (fix.diff:11, 20, 27)
services: redis-server for the Elixir PubSub tests (.travis.yml:3-4)
O10_build.project_tests: test/phoenix/presence_test.exs:36-97 covers only the Elixir tracker / group / broadcast path; no JavaScript test file or runner exists at the pinned commit (brunch-config.js:26 watches test/static, which does not exist, and package.json has no scripts)

j.j_sites_touched: assets/js/phoenix.js (constructor, static syncState, static syncDiff, new toNullProtoObj) and the identical four hunks in assets/js/phoenix/presence.js; neither path exists at the pinned commit, whose only client source is web/static/js/phoenix.js and contains no Presence
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(...) guard (or skip keys named after Object.prototype members) at the two existence checks instead of giving every presence-keyed object a null prototype: `state['__proto__'] = newPresence` still writes through the prototype on a plain object, Presence.map/list still enumerate inherited names, and real users whose ids are 'constructor'/'toString' disappear; switching wholesale to a Map fixes the collision but breaks the documented lower-level static API (fix.diff:217-218).

out_of_scope_notes: priv/static/phoenix.js:1-1026 is the compiled UMD copy of web/static/js/phoenix.js and is the published npm entry (package.json:3, 12); at the pin it contains no Presence, so it is not a second vulnerable site today, but any re-pinned 1.2-era task would inherit it as a second copy that needs regenerating.

lib/phoenix/presence.ex is the server-side producer; it groups with Elixir maps and Map.update (lib/phoenix/presence.ex:117-125), which have no prototype chain, so the Elixir half is structurally immune and is not a second vulnerable implementation.
unverified: Repository size in MB could not be measured (no shell in this session), so the tiny_repo/giant_repo thresholds are untested and neither is flagged; the tree is ~207 tracked files of Elixir and JavaScript text.

The pin is the direct parent of the first listed commit 2270aaf ("Add Presence to phoenix.js"): its hunk context, the pinned Ajax.states line at web/static/js/phoenix.js:692 and package.json's 1.1.3-era content with no mocha, match exactly. The security hunks instead target assets/js/phoenix.js and assets/js/phoenix/presence.js, files from later directory layouts that do not exist in this tree; whether the pipeline has a correct parent commit for any of them was not checkable offline.

Because of that, O1-O8 describe the advisory at the fix diff's own tree; at the pinned commit every count is zero, since a case-insensitive search of the whole tree for 'presence', 'syncState' and 'syncDiff' matches only lib/phoenix/presence.ex and test/phoenix/presence_test.exs.
O8 is empty and no latest_where is given: no later tree or release was supplied ('latest release: none'), so present_in_latest was not established for anything.
